en: To keep something at a low level; or to keep a person or group under control.
ex: The government is trying to hold down prices.
政府正試圖壓低物價。

en: To have a bad opinion of someone.
ex: Don't think ill of him just because he's quiet.
別因為他安靜就對他有不好的看法。

en: To end a relationship or an agreement with someone.
ex: She broke with her old friends after the argument.
吵架之後她與老朋友斷絕了來往。

en: To pretend to be something you are not; or to exaggerate in order to impress people.
ex: He's not really hurt; he's just putting it on.
他並沒有真的受傷，只是在裝樣子。

en: To remove things from a place, especially dishes from a table.
ex: Please clear away your toys before dinner.
晚飯前請把你的玩具收拾好。

en: To receive or get something, especially criticism or blame.
ex: The film came in for a lot of criticism.
這部電影招來許多批評。

en: To arrange or spread things so they can be seen easily; or to plan a design; or to spend a lot of money.
ex: She laid out the maps on the table.
她把地圖攤在桌上。

en: To investigate something; or to find out about something.
ex: The police promised to see into the matter.
警方承諾會調查此事。

en: To begin suddenly, especially something unpleasant such as a war or a fire; or to escape from a place.
ex: War broke out in 1939.
戰爭於一九三九年爆發。

en: To make a very great effort to achieve something.
col: lay oneself out for the prize
ex: She laid herself out to make her guests comfortable.
她竭盡全力讓客人感到舒適。

en: To begin a journey; or to start doing something with a particular aim; or to arrange things in order.
ex: They set out at dawn for the mountain.
他們黎明出發前往山區。

en: To leave home to do something social; or to stop burning or shining; or to stop working.
ex: The lights went out during the storm.
暴風雨期間燈熄滅了。

en: To disappoint someone by failing to do what they expected; or to lower something.
ex: I don't want to let you down.
我不想讓你失望。

en: To make a person or animal so frightened that they run away.
ex: The dog scared away the thief.
那隻狗嚇跑了小偷。

en: To move backward away from something; or to decide not to do something.
ex: He drew back when he saw the snake.
他看到蛇時往後退。

en: To run in different directions; or to be busy doing many things.
ex: The kids ran around in the garden.
孩子們在花園裡跑來跑去。

en: To send something to a place where it will be dealt with, especially an application.
ex: Please send in your application by Friday.
請在週五前送交申請書。

en: To become popular; or to understand something.
ex: The new game really caught on.
這款新遊戲真的流行起來了。

en: To pay a large amount of money; or to let out a rope.
ex: The company paid out millions in compensation.
公司賠付了數百萬元。

en: To suddenly start doing something, such as laughing or crying; or to speak loudly and suddenly.
ex: She burst out crying when she heard the news.
她一聽到消息就突然哭了起來。

en: Used to tell someone to hurry up or to encourage them; or to make progress; or to start to work.
ex: Come on, we're going to be late!
快點，我們要遲到了！

en: To accept something unpleasant without complaining.
ex: I can't put up with this noise any longer.
我再也無法忍受這種噪音了。

en: To meet someone by chance; or to experience something, especially a problem; or to hold a meeting with someone.
ex: Their plan met with a lot of opposition.
他們的計畫遭遇許多反對。

en: To begin doing something, especially with a particular method.
col: go about it the wrong way
ex: How should I go about finding a new job?
我該怎麼著手找新工作？

en: To cause something to happen, especially something unpleasant or surprising.
ex: The decision gave rise to a lot of arguments.
這個決定引起了許多爭論。

en: To get great pleasure from doing something.
ex: She takes delight in cooking for her friends.
她樂於為朋友下廚。

en: To be harmed, killed or affected by something bad.
ex: Many elderly people fall victim to scams.
許多老年人成為詐騙的受害者。

en: To look at the things or people around you; or to look at different places before choosing something.
ex: We looked around the old town for an hour.
我們在老城區逛了一個小時。

en: To take control of something or become responsible for it.
ex: She took charge of the whole project.
她負責整個專案。

en: To drop from a place; or to become detached; or to decrease in amount.
ex: A button has fallen off my shirt.
我襯衫掉了一顆鈕釦。

en: To arrange to do something later than planned; or to make someone not want to do something.
ex: The match was put off because of rain.
比賽因下雨而延期。

en: To get rid of something you do not want; or to waste an opportunity.
ex: Don't throw away your old books; donate them.
別丟掉你的舊書，把它們捐出去。

en: To enter a building by force, especially to steal; or to interrupt a conversation; or to make something such as new shoes comfortable.
ex: Thieves broke in and stole the laptops.
小偷闖入並偷走了筆記型電腦。

en: To suggest an idea, plan or person for consideration.
ex: She put forward a new plan at the meeting.
她在會上提出了一項新計畫。

en: To remove something from a surface by scraping it.
ex: He scraped the ice off the car window.
他把車窗上的冰刮掉。

en: To leave your bed after sleeping; or to stand after sitting or lying down.
ex: I get up at six every morning.
我每天早上六點起床。

en: To work together with someone to achieve a shared goal.
ex: The two companies joined hands to launch the product.
兩家公司攜手推出這項產品。

en: To be reasonable or logical; to be what you would expect.
ex: It stands to reason that he'd be tired after the trip.
他旅行後很累是理所當然的。

en: To go from place to place; or (of news) to become known to many people; or to avoid a problem.
ex: It's easy to get around the city by subway.
搭地鐵在市區到處走很方便。

en: To follow a plan, rule or promise exactly; or to stay on a particular path.
ex: Please keep to the speed limit.
請遵守速限。
